program: Prospective San Pablo corridor safety and finite activity access across the whole organization

nutshell.headline: Stronger local injury data, but an unproven donor contribution
nutshell.body: Signed subjective mixture: $19,089,888 per 10 Bay QALYs. Central scenario: $104,277,379. Whole organization cost is retained while two health pathways are quantified; this is not complete expected value.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: An unresolved corridor design can affect many users. Bike East Bay also teaches cycling skills, which may enable additional activity for some people.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: The public agencies already plan safety work. Historical corridor injuries are not all preventable or donor-attributable, and education attendance is not measured additional health.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Not a competitive giving recommendation on this evidence. Need a concrete additional technical task, design-specific residual risk and a credible cash response. Historical staff giving is a discovery lead, not GiveWell endorsement.

summary.label: WHOLE EXPENSE
summary.detail: 2024 functional expense plus separately netted event and inventory costs.

summary.label: BAY MIXTURE
summary.detail: Per 10 Bay QALYs; signed, subjective and partial-health.

summary.label: CENTRAL

programSection.body: The legal recipient is East Bay Bicycle Coalition, doing business as Bike East Bay, EIN 94-2585652. It provides education, events, technical street-safety work and other cycling programs in Alameda and Contra Costa counties. It is distinct from Marin and Silicon Valley bicycle coalitions.

steps.title: Use historical injuries as a scale anchor
steps.detail: CCTA's current project page provides a defined corridor and time period. Convert its fatal and severe-injury counts into annual historical rates, then remove risk expected to be addressed by existing projects.

steps.title: Require actual implementation change
steps.detail: An annual cohort of technical work receives only a share of an additional design change, conditional on implementation. Agencies, other organizations and Bike East Bay's past/future work retain their own contributions.

steps.title: Model finite, additional activity
steps.detail: Historical education attendance becomes activity only after judgments for additional cycling, alternative exercise, repeated participants, finite utility and overlap.

steps.title: Charge the whole organization
steps.detail: Keep all programs, overhead, events and netted expenses. Other benefits remain unquantified—not zero. Public construction and volunteered resources are not fully priced.

programSection.boundary: No completed lanes, petitions or countywide population totals are treated as donor-created health. One annual budget receives a finite project share, not repeated credit for the same project every year. Physical activity excludes road-injury health already counted. No electoral-persuasion pathway is modeled.

model.headline: $19,089,888 per 10 Bay QALYs
model.body: Weighted finite Bay health per annual-budget equivalent is 0.9996889638491746 QALYs; $10,000 yields 0.005238375513712699 Bay QALYs. Central finite Bay health is 0.18301140860764387 per budget equivalent. These are scenario outputs, not observed outcomes or available packages.

equation.label: Finite whole-gift health
equation.expression: gift / whole expense × cash response × Bay share × [(historical annual fatal/severe burden × current-risk scale × residual share × net reduction × discounted advantage-years × annual-work contribution × realization) + additional activity × finite utility × nonoverlap − residual harm]

inputs.label: Whole accounting resource expense
inputs.basis: 2024 original return, including event and inventory costs netted outside Part IX. Noncash resources are not automatically added again. Not a 2026 budget or full public-construction cost.

inputs.label: Five-year corridor injury anchor
inputs.basis: CCTA reports July 2020–June 2025 on its 5.5-mile Contra Costa segment. Counts are people, not county totals; raw SWITRS records were not independently extracted.

inputs.label: Current untreated risk versus history
inputs.basis: Historical traffic and reporting, pandemic conditions and future travel can differ. This is a judgment, not a forecast inferred from one year.

inputs.label: Risk remaining beyond existing improvements
inputs.basis: Separately removes the impact of completed/committed corridor work, including Del Norte and Caltrans baseline. Not a measured segment-weighted estimate. Do not simply remove miles: injuries are not uniformly distributed.

inputs.label: Finite loss per fatal/severe injury
inputs.basis: Integrated finite remaining health/disability priors, disjoint fatal and nonfatal people. No local age/severity utility data. Never multiply by another lifetime horizon.

inputs.label: Net safety-burden reduction
inputs.basis: Judgment includes design transfer and local severity effects. FHWA overall-crash results do not establish a mortality reduction here. Main rate covers existing corridor exposure; residual harm separately covers induced/displaced exposure.

inputs.label: Counterfactual advantage and delay
inputs.basis: Integrate annual burden over a finite advantage window discounted at 3%; alternative design eventually catches up. This is not the whole asset life. No selected construction date verified.

inputs.label: Annual work cohort contribution
inputs.basis: Conditional contribution of one annual budget's technical work, diluted by agencies, partners and Bike East Bay's own past/future work. No credit for entire multiyear organizational effort.

inputs.label: Actual implementation probability
inputs.basis: Additional design must be built within modeled timing. Separate from contribution conditional on implementation. Current planning is not construction approval.

inputs.label: Education participant equivalents
inputs.basis: Original 2024 report: 1,158 adults/children at 81 classes. Future scale .75–1.2 is judgment. Attendance not a verified unique treatment cohort.

inputs.label: Net additional active people
inputs.basis: First fraction must include within-cohort repeat-person/activity-period adjustment and changed cycling; second removes substitute exercise/access. Not probability of health response; not imported trial ITT.

inputs.label: Short-term activity utility
inputs.basis: Generic finite preference-weighted proxy, not a measured fitness-to-QALY conversion. Additional nonoverlap .8 central (.5–.8) removes duplicated health periods, particularly across road and activity pathways.

inputs.label: Ordinary-gift additional work
inputs.basis: Additional work after public/private funding substitution and capacity limits. Not empirically verified funding room and not a second implementation probability.

inputs.label: Bay share
inputs.basis: Local exposure but not every traveler is a resident. Same share applied to harms; no headquarters-based 100% assumption.

inputs.label: Other added adverse health
inputs.basis: Induced cycling exposure, displaced traffic or other adverse health beyond the modeled treated-corridor net effect. Do not duplicate injuries already reduced in the main pathway.

inputs.label: Joint subjective worlds
inputs.basis: Declared before first run; no empirical calibration or target-price tuning.

model.giftHeading: $10,000 illustration—not a priced additional lane, course or package

sensitivity.headline: No positive finite price
sensitivity.detail: 20% weight; zero modeled clinical gain and harm.

sensitivity.headline: $104,277,379 per 10 Bay QALYs
sensitivity.detail: 20% weight. Road Q 0.49738583828480576 + activity Q 0.06948 − harm 0.1, then funding .4 and Bay .98.

sensitivity.headline: $1,900,531 per 10 Bay QALYs
sensitivity.detail: 10% weight; 10.041379927965206 finite Bay QALYs per budget equivalent.

sensitivity.headline: $163,555,157 per 10 Bay QALYs
sensitivity.detail: No corridor benefit; activity and whole cost/harm remain.

sensitivity.headline: $24,933,077 per 10 Bay QALYs
sensitivity.detail: No physical-activity benefit; safety and whole cost/harm remain.

sensitivity.headline: $17,080,586 per 10 Bay QALYs
sensitivity.detail: Removing all adverse-burden priors still does not reach $1M.

sensitivity.headline: $34,189,261 per 10 Bay QALYs
sensitivity.detail: Halve the residual-risk fraction in every world; no other inputs changed. This is a stronger existing-project baseline, not a measured revised effect.

sensitivity.headline: $13,451,413 per 10 Bay QALYs
sensitivity.detail: Set nonnull-world funding response to1; funding-null remains0.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Whole-cost partial-health model, not complete portfolio expected value. Favorable share 100.445% exceeds signed total because other worlds subtract health; it is not a probability. No declared world is below $1M/10 Bay QALYs, but this does not establish zero real-world probability. Stronger injury data improve the exposure anchor, not donor attribution. Future technical implementation, education activity and utility remain uncertain. Unquantified other programs could materially change the conclusion.
model.fundingBoundary: 2024 revenue $1,845,171; deficit $52,605; government contributions $684,673; reported noncash contributions $54,983; net assets $732,835; liabilities $115,390; cash/savings $635,662. These are historical, not verified 2026 unrestricted capacity. Current financials page links a 2025 impact report, but its PDF was not retrieved in this pass; latest original filing found was2024. No current priced extra staff/design task verified. Agency capital, maintenance, partner staff and donated time are not fully monetized; completeResourceCostPer10 is null. No donor receives all corridor benefits or free construction. Official site has donation navigation, but checkout/restriction terms not inspected; donationUrl omitted.

evidence.transfer: Historical accounting, not marginal donor capacity or program-only spending.

evidence.population: 5.5-mile Contra Costa San Pablo corridor, July2020–June2025
evidence.result: 6 deaths and35 severely injured people; future recommendations still under development.
evidence.transfer: Defined exposure scale, not a causal effect or all preventable burden. Existing projects require residual adjustment.

evidence.result: Some improvements completed or funded; others still planned.
evidence.transfer: Do not merge different segments or claim all22miles as new. Broad campaign establishes relevance, not commissioned work on the precise CCTA task.
Not a fatality RR, not all protected designs, and not the exact CCTA layout.

evidence.population: 12 road diets and25comparison sections in California/Washington
evidence.result: Approximately6% frequency reduction; no significant rate effect.
evidence.transfer: Observational selection/exposure limitations and heterogeneous effects support null/harm uncertainty.

evidence.result: Knowledge improved but cycling/active commuting did not change.
evidence.transfer: Attendance/skills cannot automatically generate sustained activity. Local adult services differ.

evidence.result: Cardiometabolic composite improved; randomized fitness difference not significant.
evidence.transfer: Plausible mechanism, not utility calibration or lifelong mortality prevention.

reservations: Historical risk needs adjustment for existing improvements and changing exposure.
Education is not observed additional physical activity.
Future public and partner resource cost is incomplete.
Favorable tail dominates; both central and favorable cases exceed $1M.
2024 finance is not a current funding ledger.
Staff giving is not an endorsement or causal evidence.
